chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has upon him (to make up) three days of the month. Is it permissible for him to delay them, or to fast them at the end of the month? He said: There is no problem. I said: Should he fast them consecutively or separate between them? He said: Whatever he likes; if he wishes, he fasts them consecutively, and if he wishes, he separates between them.
ai.seo_question: Can missed fasts be made up separately or must they be consecutive?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the flexibility in performing qada (makeup) fasts is highlighted, specifically addressing the permissibility of delaying the three days until the end of the lunar month. The Imam confirms that whether the fasts are observed consecutively or separately is a matter of personal preference, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (yusr) in acts of worship. This ruling is particularly significant in al-Kafi as it clarifies the procedural aspects of fulfilling obligatory fasts outside of Ramadan.
